root: ^Fenlora: Forgive the rush. I would gladly share more words with you, but the gate lies ahead. We must reach it before Balbino lays his hands on the stone.
^What will I face in the temple?
^This stone... is it truly said to bind the orcs’ god?

c-0: ^Fenlora: The temple is guarded by the creatures of the forest. They heed no master, nor any plea — to them,
^ every outsider is an intruder. You are our ally, but they will not see it.
^Fenlora: Yet I trust your strength and your wit. Whether you cut a path through them or move unseen,
^ keep this in mind: the task is not glory, but reaching the stone.
c-1: ^Fenlora: I serve as guardian, chosen by our people for this century. My path is not the usual one among my kin:
^ I trained as an engineer, drawn to stonework, bridges, and turning wheels, while most of my folk devote themselves to magic or alchemy.
^Fenlora: Some think it an odd calling, yet these hands have kept our homes strong through storm and flood,
^ and our rivers steady in their course.
^Fenlora: It may seem modest work, but it matters. Still… we cannot linger here. The half-orc’s trespass weighs on my thoughts.
c-2: ^Fenlora: Legend and truth are woven too tightly to tell apart.
^ The stone was gifted to us long ago by a woman named Concordia, of Cecily Town.
^ Its first making we do not know — yet for centuries its light has guarded our forests.
^Fenlora: The orcs are quick to kindle wars from rumor and falsehood.
^ We, by contrast, have never raised steel against dwarf, nor man, nor even orc without cause — and history remembers this.
^Fenlora: So I ask you: if they cry that the stone is theirs, why should we place our faith in their word alone?
